correctness.rationale: Induction gives empty-team and union preservation for each of the first two arrows: a true universal antecedent test on the union is true on both parts; indicative consequents then combine by union, and epistemic-conditional consequents combine by splitting each tested subteam into its intersections with those parts. Lax split preserves union by combining witnesses, which may overlap. For either arrow, the classical test excluding v followed by an arrow to bottom is satisfied exactly by the empty team or a team containing v. Conjoining these tests for v in S with the flat restriction T subset S gives just empty and S. Lax splitting over all nonempty allowed teams generates exactly their unions, with bottom covering the property containing only the empty team. A two-valuation exact-team example is not flat and witnesses sharpness; for empty vocabulary there is exactly one valuation and both admissible properties are flat. For the third arrow on flat input truth sets C,D, a singleton witnesses failure exactly when T intersects C minus D, so the result is flat with truth set (V minus C) union D. Induction therefore covers all counterfactual nesting depths.
residual_risks: The reported 5100 normal-form and 340 flat-counterfactual comparisons were not rerun. The all-finite-vocabulary conclusion is analytic; no bound on succinctness, infinite-team normal form or strict-split equivalence is inferred.

value.rationale: This settles a natural language-design question raised when these weak operators were introduced. The two nonflat operators individually generate the entire finite union-closed empty-team fragment with only flat inputs to one conditional layer, whereas unrestricted nesting of the third does not increase expressivity. The sharp cutoff identifies exactly how much conditional syntax gives the gain, rather than merely providing a new name for a union-closed logic.
residual_risks: This is an expressivity and depth result, not an optimal-size translation or complexity bound. The flat branch alone is a routine consequence and is not the value basis.
